correctness.rationale: Counting (y,z) base values with multiplicity in residue dr gives D(n) by a prefix count, so g_p is max_r(T_r−a) for the (p+1)st base T_r. The rows y+2z=r+ka have step a, lengths floor((r+ka)/2)+1 and starts a ceil((r+ka)/2)+d(r+ka). These formulas reproduce the frozen parity inequalities. With U=a(p+m)+(2a−1)d, rows 0–1 already suffice when p<K_r; otherwise their entries lie below U and row 2 supplies the missing counts. This does not sort the rows globally. In r=a−1, row 1 reaches U and row 2 starts U+a(a+d−p), so exactly p entries precede U, even at the tie p=a+d. At p₀=a+d+1, lower U by a−2d. Rows 0–1 plus the first needed row-2 entries work when p₀≥K_r. When p₀<K_r at most one of the previously counted row-1 entries exceeds the reduced threshold (the reduction is strictly less than the step a), and L₂(r) is below the threshold by at least 2d. For r=1, the reduced threshold is the relevant row-2 entry and L₃(1) is one full step above it; the immediately preceding residue point has at most p₀ entries. This gives equality and the change from residue −d to d. Coprimality makes a=2d impossible. Independently checked all 2817 levels and their maximizer residues across 147 coprime pairs via direct base histogram and residue prefix sums, with a terminal block of a consecutive counts exceeding p₀ to certify each finite tail.
residual_risks: Finite replay is supplemental only. No maximal-left-endpoint claim or formula beyond p₀ is supported or required.
